text: You can create a data factory two ways — quickly, from Data Factory Studio itself, or with more advanced options, straight from the Azure portal. This lesson walks the portal path, since it's the one you'll actually use most once you're building real infrastructure alongside other Azure resources.

Every Azure resource starts the exact same way: its own dedicated page in the portal, with a Create button sitting right there in the toolbar. Data factories are no different — select Create, and the real configuration begins.

The creation form asks for four real decisions. Resource group, an existing one or a brand new one, just a container Azure uses for billing and management. Region, which is where the data factory's metadata lives — not necessarily where your actual data does. Name, which has to be globally unique across every Azure customer, not just your own subscription. And Version, where you'll always select V2.

Once creation finishes and you select Go to resource, you land here — the data factory's own overview page in the portal. This is Resource Manager's view of the resource itself: status, location, access control. It's not where you build anything yet — for that, you select Launch studio.

Launch studio opens the real authoring tool: Azure Data Factory Studio itself, where you'll spend nearly all of your time for the rest of this course. Four home-page tiles greet you immediately — Ingest for the Copy activity, Orchestrate for pipelines and control flow, Transform data for mapping data flows, and Configure SSIS for legacy packages.

One common snag worth knowing before you hit it yourself: if the browser gets stuck on Authorizing right after Launch studio, it's almost always a third-party cookie block — clear it, or add a specific exception for login dot microsoftonline dot com. Next: a proper tour of Data Factory Studio itself, tile by tile, before we build anything real.
